report.source_text: No evidence of lymphoma. Extensively necrotic fibrocollagenous tissue fragment showing mixed inflammation with predominance of neutrophils and eosinophils and collections of macrophages. Some evidence of vessel injury around the area of necrosis. Prominent necrotising lymphadenitis with karyorrhoectic debris and some palisading histiocytes, but no true granuloma formation. The surrounding mesenteric fat extensively infiltrated by lymphocytes, eosinophils and abundant histiocytes (but with no Langerhans cells). Early fibroblastic proliferation and evidence of damage to the mesenteric vessels noted.
